decision.reason: The safe mutex-backed prototype has a non-overlapping regression against the production ArrayQueue in the 64-producer corrected exporter workload. The gate requires the safe candidate to win or tie every required axis. One named regression is terminal, so unmeasured scheduler, channel-tail, fairness, cancellation-latency, allocation, RSS, physical 32/64-core, and Apple Silicon cells cannot turn this candidate into a passing cutover.

gate.candidate_rule: A safe candidate must win or tie every required axis unless an owner explicitly accepts each named regression.
gate.early_stop_rule: A statistically separated candidate regression on a real production-backed workload is terminal KEEP because the conjunctive pass rule can no longer be satisfied.

claim_time_drift.mpsc_current_fact: channel/mpsc uses parking_lot::Mutex<ChannelInner<T>> with VecDeque<T> and explicitly rejects a split lock-free queue because reservation, waiter removal, commit, cancellation, and wake state must linearize together

surface_inventory.semantics: Unbounded MPMC FIFO with best-effort count and publication snapshots; browser wasm uses Mutex<VecDeque>.
Unbounded global blocking-task queue plus cohort queues participating in dispatch, spill, cancellation, and shutdown.
Deferred cleanup work queue with size, backpressure, batch, and cleanup accounting.
Deferred cleanup-entry queue coupled to epoch and memory accounting.
Bounded FIFO with atomic drop-oldest replacement and dropped-item accounting.

benchmark_correction.shared_semantics: Capacity 1000, drop oldest on overflow, return dropped item, count drops, FIFO dequeue.

reasons: It benchmarked a hand-written ArrayQueue approximation rather than the production BoundedExportQueue.
Its manual pop and push overflow path was not the production force_push algorithm.
Its total operation count increased with producer count.
Its two-sample quick estimates cannot support tail-latency claims.
historical_harness_replay.observation: The approximation was slower than the mutex at every 1/2/4/8/16-producer cell, directly contradicting the benchmark file's old unqualified 10x+ purpose statement without measuring the current production queue.

formal_execution.command: RCH_WORKER=ovh-a RCH_REQUIRE_REMOTE=1 rch exec --base HEAD --clean-overlay --overlay-path benches/otlp_queue_contention.rs -- env CARGO_INCREMENTAL=0 CARGO_PROFILE_BENCH_DEBUG=0 RUSTFLAGS='-D warnings -C debuginfo=0' CARGO_TARGET_DIR="${RCH_TARGET_BASE:-${TMPDIR:-/tmp}}/rch_target_queue_safe_current_otlp" cargo bench -p asupersync --bench otlp_queue_contention --features criterion-benches

evidence_gaps_after_stop.detail: The admitted fleet exposed at most 16 logical CPUs. The 32- and 64-producer rows are explicitly oversubscribed and are not 32- or 64-core results.
No admitted Apple Silicon worker was available.
Criterion reports whole-workload estimate intervals here, not per-operation latency quantiles.
The exporter workload checks aggregate completion, not per-producer service distribution.
The synchronous exporter queue has no cancellation or shutdown protocol; those axes belong to scheduler and channel workloads.
No allocator counter or process-residency recorder was attached.

evidence_gaps_after_stop.axis: isolated queue cost and end-to-end exporter service
evidence_gaps_after_stop.detail: The timed region includes queue construction, payload allocation, and thread spawn/join around production queue operations. It is neither a pure operation-cost benchmark nor a full exporter service run.
The conjunctive candidate gate had already failed; these remain required before any future cutover reconsideration.

no_claims: No crossbeam-queue removal, production cutover, or new queue implementation is authorized.
The corrected exporter result does not prove scheduler, blocking-pool, epoch, or channel behavior or performance.
The corrected benchmark is a synthetic production-queue contention workload, not an isolated operation-cost or end-to-end exporter-service result.
Producer-thread counts are not physical-core counts; 32 and 64 producers were oversubscribed on 16 logical CPUs.
No p50, p95, p99, p999, fairness, starvation, cancellation-latency, allocation, RSS, Apple Silicon, broad workspace health, release-readiness, or no-regression claim is made.
No unsafe code was added and no hand-written lock-free queue is authorized.
